newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm policy paper to discuss sweeping reform.
newsitem.headline: EU farm policy paper to discuss sweeping reform.

text.p: EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is preparing a major reform of the European Union's Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) to be set out in a policy paper in the autumn, a Commission official said.
"No one in the Commission will call it reform. It is a continuing process of adjustment to the 1992 reform of the CAP," the official said.
The idea of reforming the CAP is opposed by those who want to keep farm subsidies at their present levels.
"Germany for example is against cutting farm subsidies," the official said.
But Fischler believes new world trade negotiations will force tight controls on farm support and will demand acceptable decoupling of subsidies from the agricultural market.
Fischler's paper will include measures to reform individual sectors in ways which do not impinge on other CAP product groupings.
Milk will most likely be the subject of price reductions under the existing quota regime with limited direct income support, announced under the Dutch Presidency of the EU.
This will be distinct from the urgent reform of the beef sector needed to avoid a massive build-up of intervention stocks because of the mad cow crisis.
Proposals for the cereals sector will be landed on the Luxembourg Presidency. This sector takes up nearly 50 per cent of the agricultural budget.
Some 13 billion Ecus of this is represented by cereal compensatory payments and other subsidies.
Fischler considers that this will be unacceptable in the world trade talks and his officials have said that the Commissioner is critical of the way only 20 per cent goes to small farmers.
